outcome: expression of epidermal growth factor receptors (EFGR) in the placenta
expression of prohibitin (PHB) in the placenta
cohort: The study included 58 pregnant women with COVID-19 infection during pregnancy and 40 healthy pregnant women as a control group.
finding: SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy was associated with a higher frequency of adverse perinatal outcomes (premature births, cesarean sections, lower Apgar scores, lower birth weight), increased placental vascular malperfusion (maternal and fetal) and hemodynamic disturbances, and overexpression of prohibitin (PHB) in the placenta.
mod_finding: A higher frequency of cesarean sections (34.4% vs 12.5%) was revealed in the group of pregnant women with COVID-19 infection.
cross-section timing: Placentas and perinatal outcomes were assessed at birth; COVID-19 infection occurred during pregnancy, predominantly in the third trimester (65.51%).
birth_weight: Newborns in the COVID-19 group weighed 3067.93 +/- 620.21 g, compared to 3617.25 +/- 354.58 g in the healthy group.
